Can we prove the business can operate safely today?
Whether the revenue-bearing processes can run without unacceptable cyber risk — and whether anything could force a shutdown today. Business terms, not server health.

Every critical process is up. The one control failure (claims, 14:02) is on a compensating control verified holding. No exposure is one step from forcing a takedown.

Claims keeps processing $220M/day. No customer impact. The contained failure can recur until PAM closes the underlying path — managed, not urgent.
What changed

Could anything force us down today?
No — all open exposure is contained & monitored.

How the exposure is calculated FAIR · Monte Carlo

The expected loss and Cyber VaR below are computed live, not opinions — a model you can defend to a CFO, an auditor, or a regulator. Method: FAIR (Factor Analysis of Information Risk) with a 50,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation over the evidenced input ranges below.

Expected loss (mean)
—
Cyber VaR (p95)
—
Tail (p99)
—
Appetite
$120M
Inputs — each traces to evidence, expressed as ranges not point estimates
Top loss drivers — contribution to expected loss
Sensitivity — what moves the answer most
  • Privileged-access (PAM) coverage — closing it cuts expected loss ~$31M
  • Recovery readiness (RTO) — each day of claims downtime ≈ $72M at risk
  • Third-party concentration — a single-vendor failure adds ~$18M to the tail
Model v4.2 · last calibrated 2026-06-20 · analyst-reviewed · inputs sourced from connected telemetry + industry loss data. Distributions and ranges, not point estimates — so the figure holds up under challenge.
Every input is evidence-linked · the model regenerates as evidence changes
